newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Wednesday on a technical correction after surges in the previous two days, traders said.
Tha annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.30 percent from 16.21 percent on Tuesday.
Turnover fell to 4.82 million lots from 11.15 million yuan. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said rates were likely to recover slightly later this week due to active trading on the domestic A share market.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up due to institutional support after successive falls in the past few months, traders said. Volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.78 million lots from 1.35 million.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, rebounded to 116.00 yuan from 113.59 yuan.
"Many institutions bought the 10-year bond, with its prices very low after continuous falls," one trader said. "This helped push up the whole market today."
Traders said the market should continue to edge up in the next few trading days. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
